newsitem.title: INDIA: Quake strikes heart of India, killing at least 35.
newsitem.headline: Quake strikes heart of India, killing at least 35.

text.p: At least 35 people were killed and about 1,000 injured when a powerful earthquake struck central India early on Thursday, flattening houses and burying many victims as they slept, officials said.

The earthquake, which measured 6.0 on the Richter scale and lasted about 50 seconds, hit Madhya Pradesh state in the heart of the subcontinent at 4.22 a.m. (2252 GMT Wednesday), authorities in Jabalpur city said.

Hospital officials in Jabalpur, about 260 km (160 miles) southeast of the state capital Bhopal, said 35 people had died and at least 1,000 were injured. Many victims died when their houses collapsed on them.
"The death toll may go up, but not substantially," Ajay Singh, a senior official in Jabalpur, told Reuters.

The tremor devastated Kosamghat village, 23 km (14 miles) south of Jabalpur and at the quake's epicentre. The village's 160 houses, mostly mud huts, were flattened, leaving the 1,100-odd citizens homeless, elder Mohan Lal Yadav said.
Forty villagers were injured but no one died as the quake struck during the night when they were sleeping outside in the early summer heat.
"Had this been a winter night, not a single person would have survived," said 65-year-old Shanti Bal.

In nearby Donda Mehgaon village, four people died and two were in serious condition. Numerous water buffaloes, used to produce milk or work in the surrounding wheat fields, were crushed in sheds, residents said.
They said no rescue officials had arrived at the villages because they were apparently concentrating on operations in Jabalpur, which has a population of nearly one million and much larger buildings.
The quake was felt across a wide swathe of India and woke up residents in the capital New Delhi, 720 km (450 miles) to the northwest.
"When the earthquake struck, it was like the sound of machines in factories," said Rajendra Bhatia, marketing manager for a pharmaceuticals firm in Jabalpur.
"The first noise of the earthquake was like a jet sweeping over us," oil trader Sandeep Kumar Sahu said.
A Madhya Pradesh government spokeswoman said: "According to our information many are still trapped under debris."
Earthquakes of force six on the Richter scale can cause widespread damage.

Its epicentre was at latitude 23.1 degrees north and longitude 80.1 degrees east, putting it in the Narmada River basin where five earthquakes of at least 6.0 on the Richter scale have occurred since 1927, the Press Trust of India said.

"At two government hospitals, Victoria and Medical College, there are masses of people along with rescue officials," Bhatia said. "Most of the people at the hospitals seem to be from villages close to Jabalpur."

Cracks appeared in the municipal corporation building in Jabalpur. A corner of the city's clock tower collapsed. Bhatia said: "Windows were shattered. There are large cracks on small houses. Some homes have collapsed. People are afraid that there may be yet another earthquake and there are rumours to this effect. But business is normal and shops have opened."
In September 1993, some 10,000 people died in neighbouring Maharashtra state when an earthquake measuring 6.3 on the Richter scale struck the Latur-Osmanabad region.
